name: The Isley Brothers
hook: A gospel trio that outlasted six musical eras, briefly employed a young Jimi Hendrix, and left behind two of the most sampled records in hip-hop.

blurb.age7: The Isley Brothers started out singing gospel, then made rock, soul and funk hits for decades. Rap songs sample their records all the time.
blurb.age13: O'Kelly, Rudolph and Ronald Isley began singing gospel together in Cincinnati in 1954 and moved through doo-wop, soul and rock, briefly employing a young guitarist named Jimi Hendrix in their backing band in the mid-1960s. They started their own label, T-Neck Records, and their 1969 hit 'It's Your Thing' and 1975's 'Fight the Power' became two of the most sampled records in hip-hop.
blurb.adult: The Isley Brothers' six-decade catalogue crosses gospel, doo-wop, rock and roll, soul and funk, and their willingness to keep changing sound, adding younger brothers Ernie and Marvin and brother-in-law Chris Jasper as an in-house rock/funk band in the early 1970s, kept them commercially relevant across every one of those eras. 'Fight the Power' (1975), a protest record about censorship on the radio, gave Public Enemy's own 1989 song of the same title both its name and, per sample-credit databases, part of its rhythm track.

signatureTracks.title: It's Your Thing
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Their self-released breakthrough on their own T-Neck label, and a widely sampled funk foundation.

signatureTracks.title: Fight the Power (Part 1)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Its title and part of its rhythm track were sampled directly on Public Enemy's song of the same name.
